headline_marked: Govt plans to [[rename RAB to SRF or SRB]] instead of dissolving it
headline: Govt plans to rename RAB to SRF or SRB instead of dissolving it
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs is drafting a new law to restructure the force under the police, while retaining members from military and other disciplined forces.
details: The government intends to keep the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) by changing its name to either the Special Response Force (SRF) or Special Response Battalion (SRB). The Ministry of Home Affairs has begun drafting a new law to facilitate this restructuring.

Under the proposed law, the unit will be function as a specialized unit of the Bangladesh Police. While the RAB name will be abolished, its members, installations, weapons, equipment, and existing cases will be transferred to the new unit.

The draft law consists of 29 sections across 9 chapters, covering formation, duties, search and arrest powers, and criminal investigation. It allows the members to be drawn from the police, armed forces, and other disciplined forces.

The new unit will be served by a Director General with the rank of Additional Inspector General of Police. The unit will be under the overall supervision of the government and the control of the Inspector General of Police (IGP).
The draft also retains the power to conduct searches, seizures, and arrests without warrants in cases involving drugs, arms, terrorism, and threats to national security.

This move comes despite recommendations from the UN, the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, and human rights organizations to dissolve RAB due to allegations of enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.

Discussions have also taken place regarding limiting the unit's operations to metropolitan areas, though some officials believe extending its reach to districts with manpower shortages is more necessary.

headline_marked: 3 arrested after [[attempted rape on moving bus]] in Savar
headline: 3 arrested after attempted rape on moving bus in Savar
summary: Police created a road blockade to stop the bus and rescue a woman after a 999 emergency call was made.
details: Police have arrested three people, including a bus driver and his assistant, following an attempted rape of a woman on a moving bus in Savar.

The incident occurred late Saturday night in the Barai Para area of Ashulia. The arrested individuals are driver Md. Imran (35), assistant Md. Musfeku Rahman (20), and an acquaintance of the driver, Md. Suman Pramanik (30).

The victim had boarded a Savar Transport bus from Gabtoli to Nabinagar. Before reaching the destination, the driver, Imran, allegedly beat and threatened to kill a male companion of the woman, forcing him off the bus.
After the companion was forced off, the assistant Musfeku, with the help of Suman, allegedly attempted to rape the woman while the bus was in motion.
The woman's companion immediately called the National Emergency Service 999. In response, Ashulia police created a blockade using another bus to stop the Savar Transport vehicle.
The woman was rescued from the bus, and Musfeku and Suman were detained on the spot. Driver Imran was later arrested during a police raid in the Barai Para area on Sunday afternoon.
A case has been filed under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act against the three suspects.
